tasks.title: Food Supported Population Steady State
tasks.prompt: Design a patch plan for city population growth that tapers births as food buffer approaches unsafe levels. Include the state fields, tick-order rule, and one invariant that prevents oscillation.
tasks.reference_answer: Track population, foodStock, foodPerPop, birthPressure, and recentFoodDelta. Apply production and consumption before births, then taper birthPressure toward zero as the food buffer falls near the reserve threshold. Invariant: projectedFoodAfterBirths must stay above the reserve floor, with hysteresis or a clamp so one surplus tick cannot trigger an oscillating growth spike.

simulation_spec.purpose: Trace how a food-buffer birth-rate patch affects population and food over a short deterministic city simulation.

scenario.change_under_test: food buffer should taper births as projected food approaches reserve floor

goals.benchmark: food stock remains bounded or enters explicit starvation state

goals.benchmark: population changes smoothly without one-tick growth spikes

goals.benchmark: only population/food state needed for this task is simulated

tasks.title: Market Price Elasticity From Stock Pressure
tasks.prompt: Specify a market-pricing update where surplus inventory lowers price pressure and scarcity raises it without runaway inflation. Include the formula shape, clamps, and what data must be cached.
tasks.reference_answer: Compute stock pressure as desiredStock divided by currentStock, then map it through a bounded elasticity curve so scarcity nudges price up and surplus nudges it down. Cache current stock, desired stock, lastPrice, and demand class per market tick. Clamp the multiplier to a floor and cap, then smooth toward the target so repeated scarcity cannot create runaway inflation.

simulation_spec.purpose: Trace whether stock pressure changes market price over time without runaway inflation.

scenario.change_under_test: scarcity should increase bounded price pressure while surplus should lower it

tasks.title: Worker Wage Productivity Tradeoff
tasks.prompt: Write the balancing rule for wages, morale, and worker productivity. The answer must explain how wage cuts save gold but reduce output if morale falls too far.
tasks.reference_answer: Lower wages reduce gold upkeep immediately, but morale should decay when pay drops below the expected wage band. Productivity stays stable inside the morale comfort range, then scales down past a threshold so extreme wage cuts reduce output and can erase the gold savings. Clamp the penalty and recover morale gradually after wages normalize.

simulation_spec.purpose: Trace wage changes through morale and productivity so gold savings have an output downside.

tasks.title: Warehouse Spoilage Food Decay
tasks.prompt: Propose the food spoilage rule for warehouses. Include how storage capacity, surplus size, and preservation upgrades affect decay.
tasks.reference_answer: Apply spoilage only to food above a safe storage buffer, with the decay rate increasing as surplus exceeds capacity. Warehouses raise the capacity band and preservation upgrades reduce the decay multiplier. The rule should decay a bounded fraction per tick so players can plan around surplus pressure.

tasks.title: Progressive Army Upkeep Scaling
tasks.prompt: Define an army upkeep curve that makes small defensive forces affordable but large armies meaningfully pressure the economy. Mention supply lines and a cap against impossible costs.
tasks.reference_answer: Use a low base upkeep per unit, then apply a progressive multiplier once army size passes defensive thresholds. Supply-line distance or disruption adds a bounded surcharge, making remote large armies expensive without punishing small garrisons. Cap the multiplier so upkeep pressures the economy but never creates impossible negative spirals from one tick.

simulation_spec.purpose: Trace army size and supply-line pressure into bounded upkeep that pressures but does not destroy the economy.

tasks.title: Resource Projection Cache Invalidation
tasks.prompt: Describe when projected resource income caches must be invalidated after worker reassignment, building completion, upkeep changes, and market price changes.
tasks.reference_answer: Invalidate the projection cache whenever a worker reassignment changes jobs, a production building completes or upgrades, upkeep modifiers change, or market prices shift. Each invalidation should mark the affected city/resource scope dirty, then recompute gross output, upkeep, trade value, and net delta before the next HUD or AI read. Stale cache values are never acceptable for spending decisions.

simulation_spec.purpose: Trace resource projection cache invalidation so economy reads update after worker, building, upkeep, or market changes.
